newsitem.title: UK: London stock exchange to stand up to competition.
newsitem.headline: London stock exchange to stand up to competition.

text.p: London Stock Exchange Chairman John Kemp-Welch said on Tuesday competition from alternative trading systems would not squeeze out central stock exchanges, but would force changes to their role.

Speaking at a conference on globalisation of the securities markets, Kemp-Welch said there was still a place for established exchanges despite the ever-increasing effect of advancing technology and deregulation on the world economy.
"The challenge for all established exchanges - wherever they are based - will be the ability to interpret the trends and seize the huge opportunities presented by globalisation," he said.
Kemp-Welch said it would be necessary to adapt the role of stock exchanges via further segmentation like the 1995 setup of an alternative market for young, fast-growing firms.
Speakers at the conference said new electronic trading systems, such as Tradepoint, posed a threat to traditional exchanges by providing cheaper trading alternatives.
But Kemp-Welch said an excellent reputation for liquidity, integrity and efficiency would allow the London Stock Exchange to hold its competitive edge.

Liberalisation of economies has led to new bourses springing up in emerging markets, while in developed countries, competition from alternative trading systems is fuelling a trend towards consolidation of exchanges.
Kemp-Welch said European economic and monetary union, should it go ahead, could create further pressure for consolidation of mature exchanges in the European Union.
